title: Structural Typing and Compatibility knowledge check

questions.prompt: How does TypeScript commonly decide whether object types are compatible?
options: Structural compatibility: the value must provide the required members with compatible types.
Only the interface and class names are compared.
Objects are compatible only if constructed by the same factory.
Compatibility is decided by checking the database schema at runtime.
questions.answer_key: Structural compatibility: the value must provide the required members with compatible types.
questions.explanation: TypeScript is largely structurally typed; specialized patterns such as branding add explicit distinctions.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Structural Typing and Compatibility”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with shape-based compatibility and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with shape-based compatibility and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Shape-based compatibility”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Structural Typing and Compatibility”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check assignability rules, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume practical implications for api design is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check assignability rules, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Assignability rules”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
